advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Widen the annotated-tag guard to cover `git tag` with -a/--annotate/-s/--sign/-m/-F and `gh api .../git/tags`, not just the literal 'git tag -a'
evidence: tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py:463: assert "git tag -a" not in _text(), "release.yml now creates annotated tags; fix the doc"
The test docstring says the doc must 'match what release.yml does', but the only check on tag type is a search for one exact substring.
Nothing else in the test checks for other ways to make annotated or signed tags (--annotate, -m, -s, git/tags API).
advisory.finding: The test's guard against annotated tags only looks for the literal 'git tag -a' in release.yml. If the workflow switched to annotated or signed tags another way (`git tag --annotate`, `git tag -m`, `git tag -s`, or a `gh api .../git/tags` call), the test would still pass and the doc's 'lightweight' claim would go wrong unnoticed.
scenarios: Someone adds a step running `git tag -m "Release v1.0.0" v1.0.0 && git push origin v1.0.0`. The test passes, but docs/releasing.md still says tags are lightweight.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the substring check with a regex over the workflow text, e.g. `assert not _re.search(r"git\s+tag\b[^\n]*\s-(a|s|m|F|-annotate|-sign)\b|git/tags", _text())`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make test_docs_tag_type_matches_workflow check the github_release run block for `--target` and for the absence of `--verify-tag`, and reject every annotated/signed tag spelling (`git tag -a/-m/-s/--annotate`, `git/tags` API), not just `git tag -a`
evidence: Test: `assert "git tag -a" not in _text(), "release.yml now creates annotated tags; fix the doc"`

release.yml:304-305 comment: "Without `--verify-tag`, `gh` creates the lightweight dispatch-version tag at the authorized run SHA." The lightweight property depends on `--verify-tag` being absent and `--target` being present.

release.yml:323: `gh release create "$TAG" --target "$SHA" --title "$TAG" --generate-notes --latest dist/*`. The test only asserts the substring `gh release create`, not `--target` or the absence of `--verify-tag`.
Absence rationale: the test checks for no other annotated or signed tag spellings (`git tag -m`, `git tag --annotate`, `git tag -s`, or a `gh api .../git/tags` tag-object write).
`assert "### Tag signing — SKIPPED (lightweight tags + attestations instead)" in doc`
`for stale in ("fires on **all** `v*` tags", "No rc-form tag may be pushed"):` / `assert stale not in doc`
docs/releasing.md is read by people, not by a parser or tool that branches on these strings, so the Rule-5 structural-artifact exception does not apply.
advisory.finding: The workflow-side check for 'tags are lightweight' only looks for the literal `git tag -a` across all of release.yml. It does not check the mechanism the doc relies on: `gh release create --target` called without `--verify-tag`. So the test stays green if the workflow starts producing annotated or pre-pushed tags in any other way.
merged_from: The doc-side checks match exact wording. The heading must appear verbatim, and the old prose is forbidden only as exact substrings. Rewording the heading breaks the test even though behaviour is unchanged. Reintroducing the wrong claim with any other phrasing passes, so the stale-claim checks only catch a verbatim revert.
scenarios: A step `git tag -m "Release v$VERSION" "v$VERSION" "$SHA" && git push origin "v$VERSION"` is added, and the create call becomes `gh release create "$TAG" --verify-tag ...`. Tags are now annotated (`-m` implies `-a`), yet `"git tag -a" not in _text()` still passes and the doc's 'lightweight' claim is silently false.
A `gh api repos/$GH_REPO/git/tags -f tag=...` call creates an annotated tag object, and the test does not detect it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Inside `run` (the github_release step scripts, so comments are excluded), add `assert "--target" in run and "--verify-tag" not in run`. Replace the `git tag -a` check with a regex over `_text()` such as `re.search(r"git\s+tag\s+[^\n]*(-a\b|-m\b|-s\b|--annotate|--sign)|/git/tags", text)` asserted to be None.
